title: Adaptive intake classifier & contracter for hosted API enterprise feature requests
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers submit high complexity Hosted API requests that mix streaming chat, multi-step tool/function calls, and structured outputs. Current intake flow treats these as generic feature asks and misses signals (SLA, PII, required fallbacks, model compatibility), causing long back-and-forths with Solutions and slower time-to-commit.

Goal: Build an 'Adaptive Intake Classifier & Contracter' that automatically analyzes incoming enterprise hosted-API requests and produces a prioritized, SLA-tagged contract recommendation. The classifier should: detect presence of streaming chat, tool/function chains, structured output schemas, data sensitivity/PII, latency requirements, and suggested deployment lane (hosted / dedicated / private). The contracter should generate a concise proposal with recommended model family/variant, latency SLO band, expected qps, fallback policy, and onboarding checklist for SE/AE review.

Why now: Increasing enterprise traction means more high-touch intake; playbooks we've used are manual and brittle. Automating classification + contract draft reduces triage latency, enables consistent prioritization, and surfaces engineering impact early (e.g., kernel scheduling needs, KV cache changes, backward compatibility).
acceptance_criteria: Classifier identifies streaming chat, synchronous vs asynchronous tool calls, and structured-output requirements with >90% precision on our training corpus (50 enterprise requests).
Classifier extracts explicit SLA signals (latency target, p50/p95, SLA tier) or infers reasonable defaults when absent, with an uncertainty score exposed to reviewers.

Contracter generates a 1-page proposal containing: recommended deployment lane, model family/quantization suggestion, expected qps and token budget estimate, canary rollout recommendation, and required infra changes. Output must be human-reviewable and editable.
Triage UI mock (Console intake wizard) shows classifier outputs and recommended contract; PM/SE/Design review flow in scope and clicking Approve creates PM ticket with prefilled fields.
Pilot with 8 enterprise inbound requests shows average triage cycle time reduced from 5 business days to 1 business day and stakeholder satisfaction >= 80% in pilot survey.
notes: We will train classifier on historical enterprise intake tickets + curated synthetic cases representing edge cases (multi-model toolchains, mixed structured outputs).
Tradeoffs: Strict automation risks false confidence. We will include uncertainty scores and always require human Approval for P1/P0 requests.
Privacy: PII detection relies on heuristics and flagged fields; all classifier logs in pilot mode must redact customer data and go through Security review (see dependencies).
Fallback: If classifier uncertainty > threshold, route to 'high-touch' lane and assign to Solutions SE immediately.
Metric instrumentation: triage latency, classifier precision/recall by signal, rate of human edits to generated contract, and blocked-by-engineering counts.
